## 1. Sri Lanka tabled the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill and the Prevention of Organised Crimes Bill in Parliament.

International rights bodies said the drafts kept vague offences, long administrative detention and weak court control, raising risks of arbitrary arrest and torture. Trade groups warned that gaps against global norms could imperil tariff‑free market access under the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">EU’s GSP+ scheme</span> (a programme that waives import duties for developing countries that implement 27 rights and governance conventions).

A UN office flagged <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">overly broad definitions</span>, military search powers and restrictions on reporting, while a watchdog said confessions to police and sweeping surveillance threatened due process. Business leaders pressed for tighter definitions, stronger judicial oversight and clearer safeguards before enactment, noting risks to investor confidence and legal certainty.

Lawyers pointed to clauses letting a ministry secretary sign <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">rolling detention orders up to a year</span> and allowing dress, tattoos or associations to infer gang membership. Petitions filed in the apex court challenged multiple sections, with hearings focused on detention, bail limits, court reporting and evidence rules.

## 2. The tax authority deferred the mandatory certificate requirement for specified transactions to April 1, 2027.

The move followed a surge in public demand for registrations after banks, motor registries and land offices began preparing to <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">enforce the rule on November 1</span>. Officials said alternative, simpler ways for registered users to obtain proof would be introduced and urged those not yet enrolled to use the online portal.

The decision was approved by the finance ministry and paused enforcement for <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">eight classes of activity</span> such as opening accounts, vehicle transfer and plan approval. Earlier, queues formed at head and regional offices despite a prior clarification that most adults would not automatically pay income tax simply by holding the identifier.

## 3. The power system operator withdrew its request for a fourth‑quarter tariff increase.

The step came after <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">improved hydro storage</span> and favourable rainfall reduced expected costs. A prior review by the regulator had already cut the proposed hike to <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">1.46% from 2.88%</span> before the operator stood down its petition after public consultations.

Earlier filings had cited a projected <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs. 4.4 billion revenue shortfall</span> for the October–December period. Stakeholders had queried hydro forecasts, capacity cost estimates, battery storage charges and fuel pricing transparency during the hearing.

## 4. The head of state warned that criminal networks were building a shadow power base as drug seizures mounted.

He said contraband valued at <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">about Rs. 224 billion</span>, including <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">over 6,500 kg of methamphetamine</span> and 4,000 kg of heroin, had been intercepted within a year. Authorities also froze assets of suspected figures and reported a haul of nearly 4.5 million illicit tablets and capsules.

Security agencies announced fresh maritime interdictions, including an offshore trawler carrying <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">more than 189 kg of narcotics</span> worth <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">over Rs. 4.2 billion</span>. The administration said new legal tools and financial investigations would target logistics, money flows and institutional infiltration.

## 5. The European Union approved a €10 million grant for a four‑year project to deepen sustainable trade ties.

The programme will support <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">green transition</span>, climate‑resilient exports and stronger institutions needed to meet international standards. Implementation is to be led by the trade ministry, with a finance agreement cleared by cabinet for signature.

## 6. Annual inflation in Colombo rose to 8.3% in October on the consumer index base year 2021.

<span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Food was up 8.8%</span> and non‑food 8.0%, with transport and housing making the largest contributions. The <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">monthly increase was 0.35%</span>, led by restaurant and travel costs, while declines in some protein items tempered food prices.

## 7. A supreme court bench ordered a police constable to pay Rs. 100,000 personally for assaulting a woman.

The ruling found a violation of the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">constitutional ban on cruel or degrading treatment</span> during an incident at a suburban station. Medical records and witness affidavits corroborated the petitioner’s account, strengthening accountability for custodial misconduct.

## 8. A regulator proposed a 1.46% tariff rise for the quarter before the system operator backed away from a price change.

The consultation paper cited a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs. 157.3 billion supply cost</span> and <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs. 154 billion expected revenue</span>, with a Rs. 1.1 billion deficit carried forward. Hydropower was forecast at <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">32.34% of generation</span>, coal at 25.68% and other renewables at 28.81%.

## 9. Reservoir managers opened spill gates at multiple dams after heavy rain increased inflows.

Warnings were issued to downstream communities as releases exceeded <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">several thousand cubic feet per second</span> at major sites. Storage data showed district variability, with Matale full and Ampara <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">below a fifth of effective capacity</span>.

## 10. Sri Lankan universities fell in a regional ranking, with employer reputation and faculty‑student ratios weighing on positions.

The top local entry dropped to <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">364th</span>, while two peers placed <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">389th and 398th</span>, each at their <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">lowest in four years</span>.
